html:
SMTO-CTR-0021 — SMTO's plan was cut off before it was finished

GUID: 375669da-9b08-4124-aec9-c9222b9255bc
Slug: task-contract-output-truncated
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • The model ran out of room while writing the plan for your request, so the plan was cut off and SMTO couldn't use it. SMTO didn't act on this request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Agent behavior › Task Contracts and raise Task Contract maximum output tokens. This sets how much the model may write for the plan, and it ran out this time.
  2. If Technical details say no visible plan text came back, set Task Contract thinking to Off in the same place. The model's hidden thinking can use up all the room before it writes any of the plan.
  3. Turn on Automatic Task Contract recovery in the same place. SMTO then retries a cut-off plan by itself with more room.
  4. Send your request again as a new message. Selecting Retry on this task keeps its old limits. Settings changes apply only to new tasks, so a new message uses the larger allowance.

What success looks like

  • The new task shows Task contract generated and starts working.

If it still fails

  • If you can't change Settings, send the copied error details (select Copy error details) and your request text to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change unrelated timeouts or budgets; only the Task Contract settings affect plan writing. Splitting a very long request into smaller ones also helps.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Task Contract generation hit its output-token limit (truncated output or no visible submission) and the saved attempt's automatic recovery was disabled or unrecorded, so no contract was accepted.

What this means

  • Failure handling sees compiler output-limit/truncation evidence and selects the output-limit message when retained recovery metadata does not justify a more specific recovery state. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • Failure handling sees compiler output-limit/truncation evidence and selects the output-limit message when retained recovery metadata does not justify a more specific recovery state.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect finish_reason, retained output and actual compiler ceiling; missing recovery metadata does not establish that recovery was disabled.

How to fix it

  • In the Task contract activity, inspect the attempt's finish reason, Generated output and effective_max_tokens. If the actual compiler ceiling was reached, raise 'Task Contract maximum output tokens', set 'Task Contract thinking' to Off (or lower its budget) when thinking consumed the allowance with no visible output, or enable 'Automatic Task Contract recovery' under Settings > Agent behavior > Task Contracts. These apply to new tasks only; Retry reuses the task's saved policy, and unrelated execution timeouts or budgets do not affect the compiler.
  • Inspect the compiler attempt and adjust Task Contract maximum output tokens for a new task when the actual compiler output ceiling was reached.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Task Contract Output Allowance: task-contracts / task_contract_max_tokens. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • An explicitly intended new attempt produces a complete submission under the applicable compiler output allowance.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
